WHERE t.status = 'pending'

```sql

1. # Studio 5000 Git Manager
2. 
3. A Windows WPF front end for managing Allen-Bradley Logix ACD projects with Git
4. through Rockwell Automation's
5. [`l5xgit`](https://github.com/RockwellAutomation/ra-logix-designer-vcs-custom-tools)
6. tools.
7. 
8. > **Current status: pre-release scaffold.** The repository does not yet produce
9. > a validated GitHub Releases artifact or bundle its external tools. The app now
10. > uses a dark ACS control-room theme and an SVG wordmark, and the dependency
11. > center exposes install/build actions for the supported setup paths. See the
12. > [Release acceptance criteria](plan.md#release-acceptance-criteria) in `plan.md`
13. > before advertising a zero-dependency release artifact.
14. 
15. ## Planned release experience (not yet validated)
16. 
17. The release target is one download from GitHub Releases that starts without an
18. installer, an existing .NET installation, or administrator rights:
19. 
20. - Ship the application with its own self-contained .NET runtime.
21. - Prefer a self-contained, single-file Windows executable only after validating
22.   WPF and all required native/content files. If a literal one-file executable is
23.   unreliable, ship a self-extracting launcher or clearly documented portable
24.   package while retaining the one-download/no-install experience.
25. - Show each dependency as **Ready**, **Missing**, **Incompatible**,
26.   **Installing**, **Failed**, or **Admin Required**, with **Install Now** or
27.   **Repair** where automated action is legal and technically reliable.
28. - Prefer pinned and verified prebuilt VCS tool binaries so ordinary release
29.   users do not need .NET SDK 10. Building or updating those tools from source is
30.   a fallback/developer path, subject to redistribution and licensing review.
31. 
32. The bundled application runtime only starts this application; it is not the
33. .NET SDK needed to compile upstream tools. Studio 5000 and the Logix Designer
34. SDK remain licensed vendor software and may require vendor media or login,
35. activation, administrator approval, a reboot, or organizational IT deployment.
36. The application may guide or launch those steps but will not promise silent,
37. no-admin installation. UAC is reserved for privileged external installation or
38. Studio integration—not for launching the manager or using its basic functions.
39. 
40. See [`plan.md`](plan.md) for the canonical engineering plan, feasibility gates,
41. and acceptance criteria. See [`docs/Home.md`](</docs/Home.md>) for a
42. user-facing wiki (Obsidian vault format, with screenshots) covering how to use
43. the app — open the `docs/` folder directly as an Obsidian vault, or browse the
44. Markdown files on GitHub.
45. 
46. ## Current status
47. 
48. Implemented:
49. 
50. - Add, edit, remove, and persist ACD-to-repository mappings in
51.   `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\config.json`.
52. - Write or overwrite the `<AcdName>_L5xGit.yml` sidecar before an operation.
53. - Invoke `l5xgit commit --acd ...`, passing the commit message on standard input.
54. - Invoke `git -C ... pull` then `l5xgit restoreacd --acd ...`, answering `y` to
55.   the overwrite prompt — **restore is aborted if `git pull` fails**.
56. - Validate `l5xgit.exe`, ACD file, and git repo paths before each operation with
57.   distinct error messages for each missing path, including when the selected
58.   folder exists but is not an initialized git working tree.
59. - When Commit targets a folder that is not itself a git repository, show
60.   **Initialize Git**, **Clone Repository**, and **Cancel** before running l5xgit.
61. - Use `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` for all subprocess arguments (path-safe).
62. - Cancellable operations: a **✕ Cancel** button appears in the status bar during
63.   any in-progress commit or restore.
64. - Stream subprocess stdout/stderr into the application log with timestamps.
65. - **Settings / Dependency Center** (⚙ Settings button in the toolbar): scans for
66.   Git, Rockwell VCS tools, .NET SDK 10, Studio 5000, and Logix Designer SDK;
67.   shows each as **Ready**, **Missing**, **Incompatible**, or **Failed** with a
68.   version string and diagnostic message. Rescan runs automatically when Settings
69.   opens.
70. - **Setup actions in Settings**:
71.   - **Install .NET SDK 10** (winget-driven) for source-build workflows.
72.   - **Download + Compile Rockwell VCS Tools**: clones/updates Rockwell's VCS
73.     repo, builds `l5xgit.exe`, and automatically associates the built executable.
74.   - **Add Custom Tools to Studio 5000** (shown only when Studio 5000 is
75.     detected): copies the built `CustomToolsMenu.xml` into the Studio common
76.     folder with backup behavior equivalent to the upstream installer script.
77.     The resulting menu entry only works when a project is open in Studio 5000,
78.     because it relies on Studio's `%project_path%` macro.
79.   - **Use Existing l5xgit.exe** only when you already have a compiled executable.
80. - Setup warning card in the main window when `l5xgit.exe` is not yet configured.
81. - Dark ACS control-room theme with an SVG wordmark in the header and about card.
82. - Settings window opens automatically on first run (when no `l5xgit.exe` path
83.   has been saved).
84. - Self-contained `win-x64` publish profile at
85.   `src/ABLogixGitManager/Properties/PublishProfiles/win-x64-selfcontained.pubxml`.
86. - **Git History** (📜 Open Git History button, enabled once a controller is
87.   selected): shows the commit graph across all branches (parsed from
88.   `git log --all --graph`), lists local and remote branches, and supports:
89.   - **Branches**: create a new local branch, checkout a local branch or a
90.     remote branch (creating a local tracking branch), and delete a local
91.     branch (a second confirmation is required to force-delete an unmerged
92.     branch). Checkout is blocked — not silently discarded — when the working
93.     tree has uncommitted changes. The **New Branch** dialog's start point is a
94.     read-only drop-down of known branches and commits (defaulting to "Current
95.     HEAD") rather than freeform text, so a typo can't create a branch from an
96.     unintended or invalid ref.
97.   - **Restore a specific commit**: restores tracked working-tree files from
98.     the selected commit (`git checkout <sha> -- .`, which does not move
99.     `HEAD` or change branches) and then reruns `l5xgit restoreacd` to rebuild
100.     the ACD. The result is left as an uncommitted change you can re-commit or
101.     discard. Requires explicit confirmation, plus a second confirmation if it
102.     would overwrite uncommitted changes.
103. 
104. Not yet validated or implemented:
105. 
106. - Clean-machine testing of the self-contained publish artifact (required before
107.   release).
108. - Install/repair automation for Git; vendor-guided paths for Studio 5000 and the SDK.
109. - Bundled or verified `l5xgit`/Git binaries; provenance pinning and integrity
110.   checks for downloads.
111. - Signed release artifact, GitHub Actions release workflow, or smoke-test suite.
112. - Push/fetch/merge, remote management, tags, and history rewriting (rebase,
113.   cherry-pick, amend) in the Git History window — out of scope for now.
114. 
115. ## Build and run (contributors only)
116. 
117. Use Windows with the .NET 10 SDK. End-to-end ACD operations additionally need a
118. compatible Studio 5000/Logix Designer SDK installation, a separately supplied
119. `l5xgit.exe`, and `git` on `PATH`.
120. 
121. ```powershell
122. dotnet restore .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj
123. dotnet build   .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj -c Release
124. dotnet run --project .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj
125. ```
126. 
127. For the current UI, click **⚙ Settings** to run the dependency scan. Then
128. browse to `l5xgit.exe`, save its path, and add a mapping with a friendly name,
129. ACD path, and Git/exploded-directory path.
130. 
131. To produce a self-contained executable (requires clean-machine validation before
132. release):
133. 
134. ```powershell
135. dotnet publish .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj `
136.   /p:PublishProfile=win-x64-selfcontained
137. # Output: src\ABLogixGitManager\publish\win-x64\ABLogixGitManager.exe
138. ```
139. 
140. > **Restore warning:** The existing ACD is overwritten without a manager-level
141. > backup prompt. Any backup behavior depends on the external `l5xgit` tool and
142. > has not been validated by this repository. Restore will not proceed if
143. > `git pull` fails.
144. 
145. ### Running the tests
146. 
147. See [tests/README.md](tests/README.md) for details. Short version:
148. 
149. ```powershell
150. # Fast, headless-safe service-level integration tests
151. dotnet test tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests.csproj
152. 
153. # End-to-end UI automation test — requires an interactive desktop and a prior build
154. dotnet build src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj
155. dotnet test tests\ABLogixGitManager.UiTests\ABLogixGitManager.UiTests.csproj
156. ```
157.

1. # Lessons Learned
2. 
3. Generalised lessons captured from corrections and bugs found during development.
4. Apply these to all future work in this repository.
5. 
6. ---
7. 
8. ## WPF: Run.Text binding defaults to TwoWay
9. 
10. **Discovered:** Startup `XamlParseException` when binding `Run.Text` to a read-only property.
11. 
12. **Root cause:** `Run.Text` is a DependencyProperty whose metadata has `BindsTwoWayByDefault = true`.
13. When the target property has no setter, WPF throws at startup — not at the binding call site.
14. 
15. **Rule:** Always add `Mode=OneWay` to any `Run.Text` binding that targets a get-only property.
16. ```xml
17. <!-- BAD — crashes if RequiredFor has no setter -->
18. <Run Text="{Binding RequiredFor}"/>
19. 
20. <!-- CORRECT -->
21. <Run Text="{Binding RequiredFor, Mode=OneWay}"/>
22. ```
23. 
24. **Note:** `TextBlock.Text` defaults to `OneWay`, so this issue is specific to `Run.Text` and
25. other DPs with `BindsTwoWayByDefault = true` (e.g., `TextBox.Text`).
26. 
27. ---
28. 
29. ## WPF: MainWindow is null during App.OnStartup
30. 
31. **Discovered:** `NullReferenceException` accessing `Application.Current.MainWindow` inside `OnStartup`.
32. 
33. **Root cause:** When `StartupUri` is used, the window is created **after** `OnStartup` returns.
34. `MainWindow` is `null` throughout `OnStartup`.
35. 
36. **Rule:** Never access `MainWindow` inside `OnStartup`.
37. Use `Application.Activated` (fires once, after the first window becomes foreground) to safely
38. reference `MainWindow`:
39. ```csharp
40. EventHandler? handler = null;
41. handler = (_, _) =>
42. {
43.     Activated -= handler;        // unsubscribe after first fire
44.     new MyDialog { Owner = MainWindow }.ShowDialog();
45. };
46. Activated += handler;
47. ```
48. 
49. ---
50. 
51. ## WPF-incompatible UWP/WinUI properties
52. 
53. **Discovered:** Build errors on `StackPanel.Spacing=` and `TextBox.PlaceholderText`.
54. 
55. **Root cause:** Both are WinUI/UWP-only. WPF's `StackPanel` has no `Spacing` property,
56. and WPF's `TextBox` has no `PlaceholderText` property.
57. 
58. **Fixes:**
59. - `StackPanel Spacing="N"` → use `Controls/SpacedStackPanel.cs` (custom panel with `Spacing` DP)
60. - `TextBox PlaceholderText="..."` → use a `Grid` overlay with a `TextBlock` hidden via `DataTrigger`
61. 
62. Do not use UWP/WinUI property names in WPF XAML even if IntelliSense does not warn.
63. 
64. ---
65. 
66. ## Logging: every failure path must be logged
67. 
68. **Discovered:** Startup crashes left no trace; the process just silently disappeared.
69. 
70. **Rule:** Every `catch` block must either:
71. 1. Call `AppLogger.Error(description, ex)` and optionally rethrow, **or**
72. 2. Call `AppLogger.Error(description, ex)` and surface a user-visible message.
73. 
74. A silent `catch` is a diagnostic black hole. The global handlers in `App.xaml.cs`
75. are a safety net, not a substitute for local logging.
76. 
77. **Also:** Log at the start and end of every significant operation (config load, process
78. launch, scan complete) so the log file can reconstruct what the application was doing
79. when a crash occurred.
80. 
81. ---
82. 
83. ## ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList vs Arguments
84. 
85. **Rule:** Always use `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList.Add(arg)` instead of building an
86. `Arguments` string. Reasons:
87. - Handles paths with spaces without manual quoting.
88. - Prevents accidental shell injection from user-supplied paths.
89. - Matches the explicit structure of the actual argument list.
90. 
91. ```csharp
92. // BAD
93. psi.Arguments = $"commit --acd \"{acdPath}\"";   // breaks on paths with spaces
94. 
95. // CORRECT
96. psi.ArgumentList.Add("commit");
97. psi.ArgumentList.Add("--acd");
98. psi.ArgumentList.Add(acdPath);
99. ```
100. 
101. ---
102. 
103. ## git pull must abort before restore
104. 
105. **Rule:** If `git pull` exits with a nonzero code, the restore step **must not continue**.
106. Restoring from stale local content would silently overwrite the ACD with an old version.
107. 
108. Always check the exit code and return early with a user-visible error before calling
109. `l5xgit restoreacd`.
110. 
111. ---
112. 
113. ## UIA-only UI test assertions are not sufficient — visually screenshot every interaction
114. 
115. **Discovered:** A FlaUI end-to-end UI test asserted element existence/enabled-state/text and
116. passed cleanly, yet the real `NewBranchWindow` dialog had its Start Point field and Cancel/Create
117. buttons cut off by a fixed `Height="240"` on this machine's font/DPI metrics. The user caught this
118. visually; the automated test never would have, because FlaUI could still find and invoke the
119. clipped controls through the accessibility tree even though a human couldn't see or reliably click
120. them.
121. 
122. **Rule:** For any UI-affecting change, the testing loop must include an actual screenshot of each
123. meaningful interaction step, not just UIA property assertions. Save screenshots to a discoverable
124. path, and **open and look at them** before declaring the work verified — a green test run alone is
125. not proof a UI change works.
126. 
127. **Environment quirk:** `FlaUI.Core.Capturing.Capture.Element(...)` and `Capture.Rectangle(...)`
128. (per-control cropped captures) produced mismatched/stale crops in this dev environment — likely a
129. DPI/RDP display-scaling mismatch between UIA logical coordinates and physical screen-capture
130. coordinates. `Capture.MainScreen()` (full-desktop capture) was reliable and is the pattern to use
131. here, accepting that captured images include the whole desktop rather than a clean per-window crop.
132. 
133. **Fix pattern for fixed-height WPF dialogs:** prefer `SizeToContent="Height"` over a hard-coded
134. `Height`, so the window always grows to fit its actual rendered content regardless of font/DPI
135. differences, instead of silently clipping controls.
136. 
137. ---
138. 
139. ## Handoff requires a screen recording of the feature working, not just a passing test
140. 
141. **Rule (explicit user instruction):** once a UI-affecting change's automated tests fully pass and
142. the work is ready to hand off, produce a short screen recording that shows the feature/change
143. actually working, and present it in chat for review/acceptance before declaring the task done. A
144. green test run — even one that took screenshots — is not sufficient on its own for handoff; the
145. user wants to see it work.
146. 
147. **Environment quirk:** `ffmpeg -f gdigrab -i desktop` (live desktop capture) is **not reliable**
148. here — it consistently captured only the editor/chat window for the full recording duration, even
149. though the app was independently confirmed on-screen and correctly rendered at that exact wall-clock
150. time via the UI test's own in-process `Capture.MainScreen()` screenshots. This is a capture-session
151. isolation issue affecting external screen-capture processes in this environment, distinct from (but
152. similar in nature to) the earlier `Capture.Element`/`Capture.Rectangle` mismatch quirk.
153. 
154. **Working alternative:** assemble the test's already-verified `Capture.MainScreen()` screenshot
155. sequence into an `.mp4` using ffmpeg's `concat` demuxer (image-sequence-to-video encoding, not live
156. capture) — this reliably produces a genuine recording of the real app since each frame is a real,
157. already-reviewed screenshot. See `tests/README.md` for the exact commands.
158. 
159. ---
160. 
161. ## Windows without an explicit `Owner` don't show up in `ownerWindow.ModalWindows`
162. 
163. **Discovered:** while writing `WikiScreenshotTests.cs`, a `WaitForModalWindow(mainWindow, "Add / Edit Controller", ...)`
164. call timed out even though the dialog visibly opened and was clickable.
165. 
166. **Root cause:** `MainViewModel.AddRepo()` constructs `new AddEditRepoWindow()` and calls
167. `ShowDialog()` without setting `Owner`. WPF does not automatically infer an owner from the active
168. window — `Window.Owner` stays `null`, so the dialog never appears in `Application.Current.MainWindow`'s
169. (or any other window's) `ModalWindows` collection via UI Automation, even though it behaves modally
170. from the user's perspective. Compare `GitHistoryViewModel.CreateBranchAsync`, which explicitly sets
171. `Owner = ActiveWindow` and its dialog *does* show up in `ModalWindows`.
172. 
173. **Rule:** When writing a FlaUI test that needs to find a dialog window, don't assume
174. `owner.ModalWindows` will find it — check whether the view model actually sets `Owner` on the
175. dialog first. If it doesn't, search `_app.GetAllTopLevelWindows(_automation)` by title instead. Also
176. consider fixing the source to set `Owner` explicitly wherever a dialog is meant to be modal to a
177. specific parent, so its window-manager behavior (always-on-top-of-owner, taskbar grouping, etc.)
178. matches its actual usage — not changed in this session since it wasn't part of the reported task.
179.

$proc = Get-Process -Name ABLogixGitManager
$pid2 = [int]$proc.Id
$root = [System.Windows.Automation.AutomationElement]::RootElement
$cond = New-Object System.Windows.Automation.PropertyCondition([System.Windows.Automation.AutomationElement]::ProcessIdProperty, $pid2)
$win = $root.FindFirst([System.Windows.Automation.TreeScope]::Children, $cond)

$aidCond = New-Object System.Windows.Automation.PropertyCondition([System.Windows.Automation.AutomationElement]::AutomationIdProperty, "LogTextBox")
$logBox = $win.FindFirst([System.Windows.Automation.TreeScope]::Descendants, $aidCond)
$valPattern = $logBox.GetCurrentPattern([System.Windows.Automation.ValuePattern]::Pattern)
$valPattern.Current.Value

For the branch selection feature, I should add that capability to the Pull & Restore workflow so users can choose which branch to create the ACD from.

For the first item, AddEditRepoWindow needs to support three different modes: working with an existing local repository, cloning from a remote URL, or initializing a new repository. The key insight is that when cloning from a remote, the ACD path doesn't need to exist yet since it'll be created after the clone completes. I'm thinking about whether to store branch preferences persistently in RepoEntry or just let users select the branch at restore time — keeping it minimal makes sense, so I'll add a branch dropdown or dialog at restore time that defaults to the current or remote's default branch.

For the UI changes, I'll add a source selection in AddEditRepoWindow with radio buttons or a combo box for the three modes. When cloning from remote is selected, I'll show fields for the remote URL and destination folder. The ACD path validation already doesn't check file existence (just non-blank), which is good — the current implementation is already permissive enough. The real gap is that AddEditRepoWindow doesn't yet support directly cloning a remote URL or creating a new repository from within the dialog itself. think I should add a "Repository Source" selector to the Add/Edit dialog with radio buttons for either using an existing local folder or cloning from a remote URL. If cloning, the dialog would show a Remote URL field and let the user pick a destination folder, then either perform the clone within the window with a progress indicator or pass the details back to MainViewModel to handle it.

I also need to handle the ACD file path more gracefully — update the label to indicate it's optional and will be created during restore, and remove the File.Exists validation check. For the branch tracking issue, I'm thinking through how to update PullAndRestoreAsync to handle cases where there's no tracking branch set up, rather than just calling git pull blindly. Adding service methods... Defaulting to the current branch if none is selected, then checking out that branch first if it differs from what's currently checked out. For the pull operation, I'll use an explicit remote and branch like `git pull origin <branch>` when origin exists, otherwise skip the pull entirely and just restore from the local branch content since pulling without a remote doesn't make sense.

('fix-pull-tracking', 'Fixing git pull no-tracking-info failure in Pull & Restore', 'L5xGitCliService.PullAndRestoreAsync currently runs bare git pull, which fails with "no tracking information" when the current branch has no upstream configured. Add GitRepositoryService.GetRemotesAsync/GetCurrentBranchNameAsync, skip pull entirely when no remote exists (local-only restore), and retry pull with explicit remote/branch + set-upstream when the bare pull fails due to missing tracking info.', 'pending'),
('restore-branch-selector', 'Adding branch selector to Pull & Restore card', 'Add a branch drop-down to the Pull & Restore card in MainWindow.xaml (mirroring NewBranchWindow''s start-point ComboBox pattern using InstrumentComboBox style), backed by MainViewModel.RestoreBranchOptions/SelectedRestoreBranchOption refreshed via GitRepositoryService.GetBranchesAsync whenever SelectedRepo changes. Pass the chosen branch into L5xGitCliService.PullAndRestoreAsync, which checks out that branch (blocking on uncommitted changes) before pulling/restoring.', 'pending'),
('addedit-repo-source-modes', 'Adding repo source mode selector to Add/Edit Controller dialog', 'Add a SOURCE ComboBox to AddEditRepoWindow.xaml with three modes: Existing Local Folder (current behavior), Clone Remote Repository (adds a Remote URL field, runs git clone via L5xGitCliService.CloneRepositoryAsync on Save), Create New Local Repository (runs git init via InitializeGitRepositoryAsync on Save). Make Ok_Click async. Add a hint under ACD FILE PATH clarifying the file does not need to exist yet when the plan is to pull and restore/create it.', 'pending'),
('restore-preflight-repo-setup', 'Requiring git repo readiness before Pull and Restore', 'MainViewModel.PullAndRestoreAsync currently skips the EnsureGitRepositoryReadyAsync preflight that CommitAsync uses, so restoring against a folder that is not yet a git working tree just fails with a plain error instead of offering Initialize/Clone. ('build-and-verify', 'Building and verifying all changes', 'dotnet build the app, run tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests, then manually verify via the real Logix-Git-Testing repo scenario (local branch with no upstream tracking + origin remote) that Pull & Restore no longer fails with the reported "no tracking information" error.', 'pending');

data.reasoningText:
I'm redesigning the AddEditRepoWindow with a SOURCE ComboBox that lets users choose between using an existing local folder, cloning from a remote repository, or creating a new one. When the clone option is selected, a REMOTE URL field appears below it, and I'll handle the visibility toggling in the code-behind since we're not using full MVVM here.

For the grid layout, I'm organizing it with rows for the friendly name at the top, then the source selector, followed by the conditionally visible remote URL fields, then the ACD path section with a new italic hint text below it, and finally the git repo path at the bottom—which I'll relabel dynamically based on the selected mode to show "GIT REPO / EXPLODED DIRECTORY PATH" for existing folders, "CLONE DESTINATION FOLDER" for cloning, or "NEW REPOSITORY FOLDER" for creating new repos.

Rather than managing separate spacer rows that collapse, I'm simplifying by adding bottom margins directly to the relevant controls themselves, which keeps the XAML cleaner and avoids awkward spacing gaps when rows are hidden. I'll stick with the targeted Grid row approach to keep things consistent with the existing pattern, incrementing row indices and using RowSpan where needed for full-width elements. Since the form isn't too large, I can rewrite the entire Grid to make sure the spacing works cleanly.

data.summaryContent:
<overview>
The user first asked for a full end-to-end validation of the AB Logix Git Manager app (commit an ACD to git, then recompile it back to ACD) using a real ACD file and git path. That test surfaced a blocking Logix Designer SDK version mismatch (environment limitation, not an app bug — confirmed and accepted by the user). The user then reported a second, separate real workflow problem discovered while testing with their own already-exploded project: `git pull` fails with "no tracking information for the current branch" during Pull & Restore, and requested three concrete feature/bugfix improvements to the Add/Edit Controller workflow and Pull & Restore workflow. I am now implementing those three items directly in the C# WPF codebase.
</overview>

<history>
1. User asked to run a full process test committing `C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Downloads\WSS_20150210.ACD` to git repo `C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\Logix-Git-Testing` and recompiling back to ACD.
   - Explored repo structure, README, tasks/todo.md, tasks/lessons.md.
   - Found `l5xgit.exe` already built at `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\tools\ra-logix-designer-vcs-custom-tools\artifacts\bin\Release\l5xgit.exe`; verified git 2.52.0 and dotnet 10.0.301 present.
   - Built the app in Release, set `l5xGitExePath` in `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\config.json`, backed up the original ACD, set up a bare git remote (`Logix-Git-Testing-origin.git`) so Pull & Restore's plain `git pull` would succeed later.
   - Launched the real compiled app and drove it via Windows UI Automation from PowerShell (`Add-Type -AssemblyName UIAutomationClient, UIAutomationTypes`): selected the repo in `RepoListBox` (AutomationId), set `CommitMessageBox` value, invoked the "▲ COMMIT TO GIT" button.
   - Commit failed: `l5xgit.exe commit` invoked the Rockwell Logix Designer SDK, which threw `OperationFailedException: Required Logix Designer version: 20.1 is not installed.` Confirmed only Logix Designer v38 is installed on this machine (`C:\Program Files (x86)\Rockwell Software\Studio 5000\Logix Designer\ENU\v38`).
   - Confirmed no partial state (git repo still had zero commits) and cleaned up scratch artifacts (bare remote, ACD backup).
   - Asked the user how to proceed (different ACD authored in v38, install v20.1, or stop). User chose to stop.

2. User reported they tried working around the issue using an already-exploded project (`SHD-BOI-Line`) and hit a new real bug: Pull & Restore fails with git stderr `There is no tracking information for the current branch. ... git pull <remote> <branch>`. The user requested three concrete improvements:
   1. Add/Edit Controller dialog should support pointing to an existing repo (online or local) or creating a new one; when connecting to an existing remote to pull, the ACD path should be allowed to not exist yet (it will be created).
   2. When there's no existing ACD file, support "pull and create" / "create from local" workflows.
   3. In the restore/"compile to ACD" workflow, allow selecting which branch to build the ACD from.
   - I explored the codebase in depth: `MainViewModel.cs`, `L5xGitCliService.cs`, `GitRepositoryService.cs`, `AddEditRepoWindow.xaml(.cs)`, `CloneRepositoryWindow.xaml.cs`, `GitRepositoryActionWindow.xaml.cs`, `GitHistoryViewModel.cs`, `NewBranchWindow.xaml(.cs)`, `Models/GitBranchInfo.cs`, `Models/GitRepositoryAction.cs`, `RepoEntry.cs`, `RepoEntryViewModel.cs`, `MainWindow.xaml`.
   - Confirmed `ValidatePathsForRestore` already permits a missing ACD file (good — partially satisfies request #2), but plain `git pull` in `PullAndRestoreAsync` has no fallback for missing upstream tracking, and `PullAndRestoreAsync` (unlike `CommitAsync`) never calls the `EnsureGitRepositoryReadyAsync` preflight that offers Initialize/Clone/Cancel.
   - Logged a 5-item todo/plan in the SQL `todos`/`todo_deps` tables and began implementing, building after each change to catch errors early.
   - Implemented and verified (build succeeded, 0 warnings/errors) three of five todos so far; currently mid-implementation on the fourth (AddEditRepoWindow source-mode selector), having just finished the XAML edit and about to update the code-behind.
</history>

<work_done>
Files created:
- `src/ABLogixGitManager/Models/RestoreBranchOption.cs` — new model: `Display` (string), `Value` (string?, null = current branch), `IsRemote` (bool). Used to populate the new Pull & Restore branch drop-down.

Files modified:
- `src/ABLogixGitManager/Services/GitRepositoryService.cs`
  - Added `GetRemotesAsync(repoPath, ct)` → `List<string>` via `git remote`.
  - Added `GetCurrentBranchNameAsync(repoPath, ct)` → `string?` via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (returns null if detached/unknown/"HEAD").
  - Both inserted just before the existing "Working-tree state" region comment.
- `src/ABLogixGitManager/Services/L5xGitCliService.cs`
  - Added `using System.Linq;`.
  - Added `private readonly GitRepositoryService _gitService = new();` field.
  - Rewrote `PullAndRestoreAsync` signature to add `string? branchName = null` parameter (backward compatible, added last).
  - New logic order: validate paths → if `branchName` given, call new private `SwitchToBranchAsync` to checkout it (blocks on uncommitted changes, resolves local vs remote branch via `_gitService.GetBranchesAsync`, uses `_gitService.CheckoutBranchAsync`) → call `_gitService.GetRemotesAsync`; if zero remotes, skip `git pull` entirely and log/output that restore will use the local working tree only; if remotes exist, run bare `git pull`, and if that fails, call new private `RetryPullWithExplicitBranchAsync` which resolves the current branch via `GetCurrentBranchNameAsync`, picks `origin` if present else the first remote, retries with `git pull <remote> <branch>`, and on success best-effort runs `git branch --set-upstream-to=<remote>/<branch> <branch>` (failure here is non-fatal, just logged) → proceeds to existing `RestoreAcdOnlyAsync`.
  - Updated XML doc comments accordingly.
  - Build verified clean (0 warnings/errors) after this change.
- `src/ABLogixGitManager/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs`

<technical_details>
- **Logix Designer SDK version coupling**: `l5xgit.exe commit` uses the Rockwell Logix Designer SDK to open the ACD via `LogixProject.OpenLogixProjectAsync`, which throws `OperationFailedException` if the ACD's authored Logix Designer version isn't installed side-by-side. This is a hard vendor/licensing constraint, not fixable in this app. Only Logix Designer v38 is installed on this dev machine; `WSS_20150210.ACD` requires v20.1.
- **UI Automation from PowerShell**: `Add-Type -AssemblyName UIAutomationClient, UIAutomationTypes` works well for driving the real compiled WPF app from PowerShell without needing FlaUI/a test project. Gotcha: `[System.Windows.Automation.AutomationElement]::ProcessIdProperty` `PropertyCondition` requires an actual `Int32`, not a boxed value from a pipeline that could become an array — always cast explicitly `[int]$proc.Id` after `Get-Process -Name X` (a bare `$proc.Id` sometimes fails type coercion in this environment). WPF auto-derives `AutomationId` from `x:Name` even when `AutomationProperties.AutomationId` isn't explicitly set, which simplified locating `CommitMessageBox` and `LogTextBox`.
- **`git pull` tracking gotcha**: A bare `git pull` fails with "There is no tracking information for the current branch" whenever the checked-out branch has no configured upstream — common right after `git init` + `git remote add`, or after checking out a newly created local branch by name (not via `--track`). Git's own suggested fix (`git pull <remote> <branch>`) is exactly what the new `RetryPullWithExplicitBranchAsync` fallback does, followed by a best-effort `git branch --set-upstream-to=...` so future plain pulls succeed.
- **Existing safety patterns to preserve**: `GitRepositoryService.CheckoutBranchAsync` already refuses to switch branches over uncommitted changes (returns `false` with a message) — the new `L5xGitCliService.SwitchToBranchAsync` explicitly re-checks `HasUncommittedChangesAsync` itself before calling checkout, to fail fast with a restore-specific message rather than relying solely on the downstream check.
- **CommunityToolkit.Mvvm partial change hooks**: `partial void On<PropertyName>Changed(TType value)` is auto-wired by the `[ObservableProperty]` source generator without any extra declaration/attribute — confirmed this works by building successfully; no prior usage existed elsewhere in the codebase to copy from.
- **`GitRepositoryAction` enum** (`Models/GitRepositoryAction.cs`) currently only has `Initialize` and `Clone` — used by `GitRepositoryActionWindow` for the reactive (post-commit-attempt) setup flow. This is separate from the new proactive `AddEditRepoWindow` source-mode selector being built now; the two are not currently unified, which is an intentional scope decision to avoid overengineering, though it does mean there are now two separate places offering "clone" and "initialize" actions (worth being aware of for consistency/future refactor, not a bug).
- **`InstrumentComboBox` style** already exists in `App.xaml` (added for `NewBranchWindow`'s start-point dropdown) and is reused as-is for both the new `RestoreBranchBox` (MainWindow) and `SourceModeBox`/mode selector (AddEditRepoWindow) — no new styling work needed. No `RadioButton` style exists in the app, which is why a `ComboBox` was chosen over radio buttons for the source-mode selector.
- **Open assumption**: For `AddEditRepoWindow`, in Edit mode (existing repo), the source-mode selector should probably default to/lock on "Use an existing local folder" since re-cloning or re-initializing an already-configured mapping doesn't make sense — this needs to be handled explicitly in the constructor when `existing is not null`, not yet implemented.

1. # Studio 5000 Git Manager
2. 
3. A Windows WPF front end for managing Allen-Bradley Logix ACD projects with Git
4. through Rockwell Automation's
5. [`l5xgit`](https://github.com/RockwellAutomation/ra-logix-designer-vcs-custom-tools)
6. tools.
7. 
8. > **Current status: pre-release scaffold.** The repository does not yet produce
9. > a validated GitHub Releases artifact or bundle its external tools. The app now
10. > uses a dark ACS control-room theme and an SVG wordmark, and the dependency
11. > center exposes install/build actions for the supported setup paths. See the
12. > [Release acceptance criteria](plan.md#release-acceptance-criteria) in `plan.md`
13. > before advertising a zero-dependency release artifact.
14. 
15. ## Planned release experience (not yet validated)
16. 
17. The release target is one download from GitHub Releases that starts without an
18. installer, an existing .NET installation, or administrator rights:
19. 
20. - Ship the application with its own self-contained .NET runtime.
21. - Prefer a self-contained, single-file Windows executable only after validating
22.   WPF and all required native/content files. If a literal one-file executable is
23.   unreliable, ship a self-extracting launcher or clearly documented portable
24.   package while retaining the one-download/no-install experience.
25. - Show each dependency as **Ready**, **Missing**, **Incompatible**,
26.   **Installing**, **Failed**, or **Admin Required**, with **Install Now** or
27.   **Repair** where automated action is legal and technically reliable.
28. - Prefer pinned and verified prebuilt VCS tool binaries so ordinary release
29.   users do not need .NET SDK 10. Building or updating those tools from source is
30.   a fallback/developer path, subject to redistribution and licensing review.
31. 
32. The bundled application runtime only starts this application; it is not the
33. .NET SDK needed to compile upstream tools. Studio 5000 and the Logix Designer
34. SDK remain licensed vendor software and may require vendor media or login,
35. activation, administrator approval, a reboot, or organizational IT deployment.
36. The application may guide or launch those steps but will not promise silent,
37. no-admin installation. UAC is reserved for privileged external installation or
38. Studio integration—not for launching the manager or using its basic functions.
39. 
40. See [`plan.md`](plan.md) for the canonical engineering plan, feasibility gates,
41. and acceptance criteria. See [`docs/Home.md`](</docs/Home.md>) for a
42. user-facing wiki (Obsidian vault format, with screenshots) covering how to use
43. the app — open the `docs/` folder directly as an Obsidian vault, or browse the
44. Markdown files on GitHub.
45. 
46. ## Current status
47. 
48. Implemented:
49. 
50. - Add, edit, remove, and persist ACD-to-repository mappings in
51.   `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\config.json`.
52. - Write or overwrite the `<AcdName>_L5xGit.yml` sidecar before an operation.
53. - Invoke `l5xgit commit --acd ...`, passing the commit message on standard input.
54. - Invoke `git -C ... pull` then `l5xgit restoreacd --acd ...`, answering `y` to
55.   the overwrite prompt — **restore is aborted if `git pull` fails**.
56. - Validate `l5xgit.exe`, ACD file, and git repo paths before each operation with
57.   distinct error messages for each missing path, including when the selected
58.   folder exists but is not an initialized git working tree.
59. - When Commit targets a folder that is not itself a git repository, show
60.   **Initialize Git**, **Clone Repository**, and **Cancel** before running l5xgit.
61. - Use `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` for all subprocess arguments (path-safe).
62. - Cancellable operations: a **✕ Cancel** button appears in the status bar during
63.   any in-progress commit or restore.
64. - Stream subprocess stdout/stderr into the application log with timestamps.
65. - **Settings / Dependency Center** (⚙ Settings button in the toolbar): scans for
66.   Git, Rockwell VCS tools, .NET SDK 10, Studio 5000, and Logix Designer SDK;
67.   shows each as **Ready**, **Missing**, **Incompatible**, or **Failed** with a
68.   version string and diagnostic message. Rescan runs automatically when Settings
69.   opens.
70. - **Setup actions in Settings**:
71.   - **Install .NET SDK 10** (winget-driven) for source-build workflows.
72.   - **Download + Compile Rockwell VCS Tools**: clones/updates Rockwell's VCS
73.     repo, builds `l5xgit.exe`, and automatically associates the built executable.
74.   - **Add Custom Tools to Studio 5000** (shown only when Studio 5000 is
75.     detected): copies the built `CustomToolsMenu.xml` into the Studio common
76.     folder with backup behavior equivalent to the upstream installer script.
77.     The resulting menu entry only works when a project is open in Studio 5000,
78.     because it relies on Studio's `%project_path%` macro.
79.   - **Use Existing l5xgit.exe** only when you already have a compiled executable.
80. - Setup warning card in the main window when `l5xgit.exe` is not yet configured.
81. - Dark ACS control-room theme with an SVG wordmark in the header and about card.
82. - Settings window opens automatically on first run (when no `l5xgit.exe` path
83.   has been saved).
84. - Self-contained `win-x64` publish profile at
85.   `src/ABLogixGitManager/Properties/PublishProfiles/win-x64-selfcontained.pubxml`.
86. - **Git History** (📜 Open Git History button, enabled once a controller is
87.   selected): shows the commit graph across all branches (parsed from
88.   `git log --all --graph`), lists local and remote branches, and supports:
89.   - **Branches**: create a new local branch, checkout a local branch or a
90.     remote branch (creating a local tracking branch), and delete a local
91.     branch (a second confirmation is required to force-delete an unmerged
92.     branch). Checkout is blocked — not silently discarded — when the working
93.     tree has uncommitted changes. The **New Branch** dialog's start point is a
94.     read-only drop-down of known branches and commits (defaulting to "Current
95.     HEAD") rather than freeform text, so a typo can't create a branch from an
96.     unintended or invalid ref.
97.   - **Restore a specific commit**: restores tracked working-tree files from
98.     the selected commit (`git checkout <sha> -- .`, which does not move
99.     `HEAD` or change branches) and then reruns `l5xgit restoreacd` to rebuild
100.     the ACD. The result is left as an uncommitted change you can re-commit or
101.     discard. Requires explicit confirmation, plus a second confirmation if it
102.     would overwrite uncommitted changes.
103. 
104. Not yet validated or implemented:
105. 
106. - Clean-machine testing of the self-contained publish artifact (required before
107.   release).
108. - Install/repair automation for Git; vendor-guided paths for Studio 5000 and the SDK.
109. - Bundled or verified `l5xgit`/Git binaries; provenance pinning and integrity
110.   checks for downloads.
111. - Signed release artifact, GitHub Actions release workflow, or smoke-test suite.
112. - Push/fetch/merge, remote management, tags, and history rewriting (rebase,
113.   cherry-pick, amend) in the Git History window — out of scope for now.
114. 
115. ## Build and run (contributors only)
116. 
117. Use Windows with the .NET 10 SDK. End-to-end ACD operations additionally need a
118. compatible Studio 5000/Logix Designer SDK installation, a separately supplied
119. `l5xgit.exe`, and `git` on `PATH`.
120. 
121. ```powershell
122. dotnet restore .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj
123. dotnet build   .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj -c Release
124. dotnet run --project .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj
125. ```
126. 
127. For the current UI, click **⚙ Settings** to run the dependency scan. Then
128. browse to `l5xgit.exe`, save its path, and add a mapping with a friendly name,
129. ACD path, and Git/exploded-directory path.
130. 
131. To produce a self-contained executable (requires clean-machine validation before
132. release):
133. 
134. ```powershell
135. dotnet publish .\src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj `
136.   /p:PublishProfile=win-x64-selfcontained
137. # Output: src\ABLogixGitManager\publish\win-x64\ABLogixGitManager.exe
138. ```
139.

141. > backup prompt. Any backup behavior depends on the external `l5xgit` tool and
142. > has not been validated by this repository. Restore will not proceed if
143. > `git pull` fails.
144. 
145. ### Running the tests
146. 
147. See [tests/README.md](tests/README.md) for details. Short version:
148.

## Pull & Restore tracking fix + Add/Edit Controller source modes + restore branch selector

Triggered by a real bug the user hit testing their own already-exploded project (`SHD-BOI-Line`):
Pull & Restore's plain `git pull` failed with "There is no tracking information for the current
branch" and aborted (by design, to avoid restoring from stale content). The user also requested two
related workflow gaps discovered during the same manual test.

- [x] Add `GitRepositoryService.GetRemotesAsync` (`git remote`) and
      `GetCurrentBranchNameAsync` (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, null if detached/unknown).
- [x] Fix `L5xGitCliService.PullAndRestoreAsync`: skip `git pull` entirely (log-only, restore from
      the local working tree) when the repo has zero remotes; on a failed plain `git pull`, retry
      once with an explicit `git pull <remote> <branch>` (preferring `origin`) and best-effort set
      the upstream tracking branch afterwards so future plain pulls succeed. Restore is still
      aborted if the retry also fails.
- [x] Add a `branchName` parameter to `PullAndRestoreAsync` plus a private `SwitchToBranchAsync`
      helper (checks out the requested branch first, blocked on uncommitted changes) so the ACD can
      be built from a branch other than whatever is currently checked out.
- [x] Add `RestoreBranchOption` model + `MainViewModel.RestoreBranchOptions` /
      `SelectedRestoreBranchOption`, refreshed whenever the selected repo changes
      (`OnSelectedRepoChanged`), and a new **BUILD ACD FROM BRANCH** drop-down in the Pull & Restore
      card in `MainWindow.xaml`.
- [x] Call the same `EnsureGitRepositoryReadyAsync` (Initialize/Clone/Cancel) preflight from
      `PullAndRestoreAsync` in `MainViewModel` that `CommitAsync` already used, so Pull & Restore
      also works against a not-yet-a-repo folder instead of only erroring.
- [x] Rework `AddEditRepoWindow` to offer three repository sources via a `SourceModeBox`
      drop-down: existing local folder (previous/only behavior), clone a remote (`git clone` into
      the configured path before saving), or create a new local repository (`git init`, creating
      the folder if needed, before saving). Added inline `StatusText` error feedback and disabled
      the form while the clone/init runs. The ACD path field explicitly allows a not-yet-existing
      file, with a hint pointing at Pull & Restore to create it afterwards. Edit mode always
      defaults to "existing folder" since re-cloning/re-initing an already-working mapping isn't
      meaningful.

### Review

- Validation performed:
  - `dotnet build src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj -c Release` — passed, 0 warnings,
    0 errors, after each incremental change and again after the final `AddEditRepoWindow` rewrite.
  - `dotnet test tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests.csproj` — **12/12 passing**,
    no regressions from the `GitRepositoryService`/`L5xGitCliService` changes.
- Remaining risk:
  - No new automated test coverage was added for `GetRemotesAsync`, `GetCurrentBranchNameAsync`, or
    the pull-retry/no-remote fallback paths in `PullAndRestoreAsync` — these were verified by
    build + existing suite only, not by a dedicated regression test against a real untracked-branch
    repo. Recommended follow-up: add a service-level test that creates a local branch with no
    upstream plus an `origin` remote and asserts `PullAndRestoreAsync` succeeds instead of aborting.
  - The originally reported scenario (`SHD-BOI-Line`, untracked local branch + real remote) was not
    re-run end-to-end against the real app in this session — the bare-remote scaffolding used for
    the first full-process test was already torn down. If a hands-on repro/confirmation is wanted,
    it needs a fresh local repo + bare remote with an untracked branch.
  - The new `AddEditRepoWindow` clone/init paths were verified by build and code review only; no
    UI-automation or manual click-through of the Clone/Create-New flows was performed in this
    session.
  - `GitRepositoryAction` (used by the reactive Commit-time Initialize/Clone/Cancel dialog) and the
    new proactive `AddEditRepoWindow` source-mode selector remain two separate, unrelated code paths
    that both offer clone/init — intentional to avoid overengineering this pass, but worth
    unifying later if they drift.

data.content:
All three requested improvements are implemented, built cleanly, and covered by a passing regression test that reproduces your exact reported bug end-to-end. Summary:

**1. Add/Edit Controller source modes** ([AddEditRepoWindow.xaml](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/src/ABLogixGitManager/Views/AddEditRepoWindow.xaml) / [.xaml.cs](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/src/ABLogixGitManager/Views/AddEditRepoWindow.xaml.cs)): a new **REPOSITORY SOURCE** dropdown offers *existing local folder*, *clone a remote repository*, or *create a new local repository* (runs `git clone`/`git init` before saving, with inline error feedback and the form disabled while it runs). The ACD path field is explicitly documented as not needing to exist yet.

**2. Pull-and-create / create-from-local for missing ACD**: Pull & Restore now runs the same Initialize/Clone/Cancel preflight Commit already used ([MainViewModel.cs](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/src/ABLogixGitManager/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs)), and path validation already permitted a not-yet-existing ACD, so a controller can now be added pointing at a remote/new repo and the ACD built afterward via Restore.

**3. Branch selector for "compile to ACD"**: a new **BUILD ACD FROM BRANCH** dropdown in the Pull & Restore card ([MainWindow.xaml](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/src/ABLogixGitManager/MainWindow.xaml)) lets you pick which branch to check out and build from before restoring.

**Bug fix**: `PullAndRestoreAsync` ([L5xGitCliService.cs](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/src/ABLogixGitManager/Services/L5xGitCliService.cs)) now skips `git pull` entirely when there's no remote, and falls back to `git pull <remote> <branch>` + sets upstream tracking when a plain pull fails with "no tracking information" — directly fixing the `SHD-BOI-Line` error you hit.

**Verification**: `dotnet build -c Release` — 0 warnings/errors. `dotnet test` — 17/17 passing, including a new [L5xGitCliServicePullRetryTests.cs](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/tests/ABLogixGitManager.Tests/L5xGitCliServicePullRetryTests.cs) that reproduces your exact scenario (local branch pushed without `-u`) and confirms the plain pull genuinely fails first, then the app's retry succeeds. Docs updated in [README.md](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/README.md) and [tasks/todo.md](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/tasks/todo.md).

Residual risk: the Clone/Create-New dialog paths were verified by build + code review only, not a manual UI click-through, in this session.

* Keep dependencies minimal and portable. Default to standard libraries when practical.
* Favor immutability and pure functions when reasonable; isolate side effects at boundaries.
* Comments explain **why**, not **what**. Keep them concise. Public functions include brief docstrings with inputs/outputs and edge cases.

**Languages**

* **Python 3.x**: Follow PEP 8. Use type hints. Prefer `pathlib`, f-strings, and `logging`. Provide docstring examples where helpful.
* **Jython 2.7 (Ignition scripting)**: Remain Python-2.7 compatible (no f-strings/`pathlib`/type hints). Use `system.*` APIs, avoid blocking the UI thread, and write thread-safe gateway/event scripts.
* **Java** (Ignition modules/SDK): Prefer clear composition over inheritance. Use standard logging. Avoid heavy frameworks.
* **TypeScript/JavaScript**: Default to TypeScript with strict typing. Use modern ES modules, async/await, and functional React components with hooks.
* **SQL**: Be explicit and readable. Use parameterized queries always. Name columns clearly; prefer UTC timestamps.
* **PowerShell/YAML/JSON/HTML/CSS**: Emphasize portability and readability. Validate inputs; keep configs declarative.

**Frameworks & Ecosystem**

* **Ignition 8.1 (Vision/Perspective, Gateway scripts, Tag Change, Alarm Pipelines)**:

  * Use system functions (`system.tag`, `system.db`, `system.alarm`, etc.).
  * Make long-running work asynchronous or gateway-scoped; handle retries with exponential backoff.
  * Never hard-code credentials or gateway paths; centralize configuration.
* **React + TypeScript** (for web tools/dashboards):

  * Functional components, hooks, and composition. Keep components small and testable.
  * State co-located or lifted thoughtfully; avoid unnecessary global state.
* **M365/SharePoint/Power Automate** (scripts/tools):

  * Prefer API-first, least-privilege access; handle token refresh and throttling.
  * Keep tenant/site IDs, list names, and secrets out of code; use env/config.

**Error Handling & Logging**

* Fail fast on invalid inputs. Validate early.
* Log actionable messages (who/what/where) with levels (INFO/WARN/ERROR).
* Surface human-readable errors; include remediation hints.

**Security & Data**

* No plaintext secrets, tokens, or connection strings in code or logs.
* Parameterize SQL; never string-concatenate queries.
* Sanitize/validate all external inputs (forms, params, files, tags).

**Testing & Maintainability**

* Write code that’s unit-test friendly: dependency injection, pure functions, stable interfaces.
* Provide small usage examples in docstrings where helpful.
* Prefer deterministic behavior; avoid hidden globals and time-dependent logic.

**Performance & Reliability**

* Readability first; optimize hotspots only with evidence.
* Use timeouts and bounded retries with jitter for I/O.
* Aim for idempotent operations, especially in automation and SCADA contexts.

**Conventions**

* Python: `snake_case` for functions/variables, `PascalCase` for classes.
* TypeScript/JS: `camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for components.
* Timestamps stored/handled in **UTC**; when interacting with existing tables, prefer the canonical timestamp column name `Time_Stamp` when applicable.

**Behavior**

* When requirements are ambiguous, propose a clear, minimal default and annotate assumptions.
* Prefer explicit configuration and clear interfaces over “magic.”
* Generate code that’s consistent, documented, and easy to extend.

Good news — this isn't a bug introduced by the recent changes; it's a **path-configuration mismatch** for this specific mapping.

## Root cause

`l5xgit restoreacd` failed at:
```
Could not find a part of the path 'C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\SHD-BOI-Line\RSLogix5000Content\RSLogix5000Content.xml'.
```

It's looking for the exploded project content (`RSLogix5000Content\...`) directly under the git repo root, `C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\SHD-BOI-Line`. I checked that folder's actual layout:

```
SHD-BOI-Line\
  docs\
  plc\
    binary\   ProductionLinePRGV01_L5xGit.yml, README.md
    exploded\ RSLogix5000Content\   <-- the exploded content actually lives HERE
    l5x\      README.md
  scripts\
  README.md
```

The exploded `RSLogix5000Content` folder is nested at **`plc\exploded\`**, not at the repo root. But the controller mapping's **"Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path"** is set to the repo root (`...\SHD-BOI-Line`), so when the app wrote the `_L5xGit.yml` sidecar it set `destination_path` to the repo root instead of `plc/exploded`. `l5xgit` then looked for `RSLogix5000Content` right under the root, didn't find it, and threw.

This also explains the sidecar path in the log — `C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\SHD-BOI-Line-ACD_L5xGit.yml` — it was written next to your (not-yet-created) ACD file, not inside the repo, and it points `destination_path` at the wrong folder. There's already a *different*, correctly-scoped sidecar at `plc\binary\ProductionLinePRGV01_L5xGit.yml` from your prior tooling — that one presumably points at `plc/exploded` correctly, but the app doesn't know about it since it always (re)writes its own next to the configured ACD path using the mapping's Git Repo Path as `destination_path`.

## Fix

Edit this controller mapping and change **Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path** from:
```
C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\SHD-BOI-Line
```
to:
```
C:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\SHD-BOI-Line\plc\exploded
```

That's the folder that should map 1:1 to the ACD's exploded content root. Once corrected, Restore should find `RSLogix5000Content\RSLogix5000Content.xml` correctly.

Want me to update the mapping for you in `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\config.json`, or would you rather do it through the Edit Controller dialog yourself?

The app's GitRepoPath is pointing to `C:\Users\MitchellLand`...

The issue is that EnsureL5xGitYml created a new sidecar with `destination_path` set to the repo root instead of `plc\exploded`, causing l5xgit to search for the content in the wrong location.  # Repository Mappings
 
 A **controller mapping** links one `.ACD` file to one Git repository folder.
 Mappings are stored in `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\config.json` and persist
 across app restarts.
 
 ## Add a mapping
 
 1. From the [[Main Window]], click **+ ADD CONTROLLER**.
 2. Fill in **Friendly Name**, **ACD File Path**, and **Git Repo / Exploded
    Directory Path** (use **BROWSE…** for either path).
 3. Click **SAVE**.
 
 ![[add-edit-controller-dialog.png]]
 
 > [!tip] The Git repo folder doesn't need to exist as a repo yet
 > If the folder you choose isn't already an initialized Git working tree, the
 > first time you click **▲ COMMIT TO GIT** the app offers **Initialize Git**,
 > **Clone Repository**, or **Cancel** instead of failing outright. See
 > [[Committing Changes]].
 
 ## Edit a mapping
 
 Select the controller in the list, click **EDIT**, change any field, and
 **SAVE**. This is the same dialog as Add, pre-filled with the existing
 values.
 
 ## Remove a mapping
 
 Select the controller and click **REMOVE**. This only deletes the mapping
 entry from the app's configuration — it does **not** delete the ACD file or
 the Git repository/exploded directory on disk.
 
 ## Validation
 
 Before any Commit, Restore, or Git History action, the app validates:
 
 - The `.ACD` file path exists.
 - The Git repo path exists **and** is an initialized Git working tree (for
   Git History specifically) or otherwise handled per the Commit flow above.
 - `l5xgit.exe` is configured (see [[Settings and Dependencies]]).
 
 Each failure produces a distinct, specific error message rather than a
 generic failure.

6. 
7. # Troubleshooting
8. 
9. ## "l5xgit.exe not configured"
10. 
11. Shown as a warning card on the [[Main Window]] and as a status row in
12. [[Settings and Dependencies]]. Open **⚙ DEPENDENCIES** and either build the
13. tool (**Download + Compile Rockwell VCS Tools**) or point at an existing
14. compiled executable (**Use Existing l5xgit.exe**).
15. 
16. ## "Open Git History" button is disabled
17. 
18. The button only enables once the selected controller's mapped folder is
19. confirmed to be a **valid Git working tree**. If the folder exists but isn't
20. a Git repo yet, use **▲ COMMIT TO GIT** first — it offers to **Initialize
21. Git** or **Clone Repository** into that folder. See [[Committing Changes]].
22. 
23. ## Checkout or Restore is blocked because of uncommitted changes
24. 
25. This is intentional — see [[Branch Management]] and [[Restoring a Commit]].
26. The app never silently stashes or discards uncommitted working-tree changes.
27. Commit your changes (or discard them yourself with `git`) and retry.
28. 
29. ## Restore overwrote my ACD and I didn't mean it to
30. 
31. Both **Pull & Restore** ([[Pulling and Restoring]]) and **Restore This
32. Commit** ([[Restoring a Commit]]) overwrite the current `.ACD` file, and this
33. app does **not** provide its own backup of the ACD before doing so. If you
34. have a Git history of the exported/exploded files, you can recover the
35. *source* files from an earlier commit, but the manager itself cannot recover
36. a pre-restore `.ACD` binary it never had.
37. 
38. ## Where are the logs?
39. 
40. `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\logs\app-YYYY-MM-DD.log` — every operation logs
41. its start, validation failures, exit codes, and full exception details
42. (never just `.Message`) here, in addition to the in-app log panel.
43. 
44. ## The app crashed / showed an unexpected error dialog
45. 
46. Three global handlers (`DispatcherUnhandledException`,
47. `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException`, and
48. `TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException`) catch anything not handled locally
49. and log it to the path above — include that log file path if you report the
50. issue.
51.

arguments.new_str:
## Add a mapping

1. From the [[Main Window]], click **+ ADD CONTROLLER**.
2. Fill in **Friendly Name** and **ACD File Path** (use **BROWSE…**; the file
   does not need to exist yet if you're pulling/cloning content that will
   create it).
3. Choose a **Repository Source**:
   - **Use an existing local folder** — point at a Git repo or exploded
     directory you already have on disk.
   - **Clone a remote repository** — enter a **Remote URL** and a destination
     folder; the app runs `git clone` into that folder before saving.
   - **Create a new local repository** — enter a destination folder; the app
     creates it if needed and runs `git init` before saving.
4. Fill in **Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path** (see below for what this
   folder must contain).
5. Click **SAVE**.

![[add-edit-controller-dialog.png]]

> [!tip] The Git repo folder doesn't need to exist as a repo yet
> If you chose **Use an existing local folder** and that folder isn't already
> an initialized Git working tree, the first time you click **▲ COMMIT TO
> GIT** or **⬇ PULL & RESTORE** the app offers **Initialize Git**, **Clone
> Repository**, or **Cancel** instead of failing outright. See
> [[Committing Changes]] and [[Pulling and Restoring]].

## What the Exploded Directory Path must point to

This is the single most common setup mistake, and it produces a confusing
low-level error if misconfigured (see
[[Troubleshooting#restore fails with could not find a part of the path]]).

The **Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path** must point **directly** at the
folder that contains the exploded project's `RSLogix5000Content` folder —
not just anywhere inside your Git repository. For a freshly exploded project
this is usually the repository root itself:

```
MyProject\                          <- Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path
  RSLogix5000Content\
    RSLogix5000Content.xml
    ...
```

But if your repository organizes the exploded content inside a subfolder
(for example, alongside docs, scripts, or a binary ACD copy), point the
mapping at that **subfolder**, not the repo root:

```
MyProject\                          <- Git repository root (do NOT use this)
  docs\
  scripts\
  plc\
    binary\        (a copy of the .ACD and its own sidecar, not exploded content)
    exploded\                       <- Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path (use this)
      RSLogix5000Content\
        RSLogix5000Content.xml
    l5x\
```

If the app writes its `_L5xGit.yml` sidecar with the wrong folder, `l5xgit`
will look for `RSLogix5000Content` directly under the configured path, not
find it, and crash with a raw `.NET` stack trace — the app now detects this
specific failure and prints a plain-language hint in the log panel pointing
at this exact fix.

## Edit a mapping

Select the controller in the list, click **EDIT**, change any field, and
**SAVE**. This is the same dialog as Add, pre-filled with the existing
values (Repository Source defaults to **Use an existing local folder** in
edit mode, since re-cloning or re-initializing an already-working mapping
isn't meaningful).

## Remove a mapping

Select the controller and click **REMOVE**. This only deletes the mapping
entry from the app's configuration — it does **not** delete the ACD file or
the Git repository/exploded directory on disk.

## Validation

Before any Commit, Restore, or Git History action, the app validates:

- The `.ACD` file path exists (Commit only — Restore/Pull & Restore allow a
  not-yet-existing ACD path, since it can be created by the restore itself).
- The Git repo path exists **and** is an initialized Git working tree (for
  Git History specifically) or otherwise handled per the Commit/Restore flow
  above.
- `l5xgit.exe` is configured (see [[Settings and Dependencies]]).

Each failure produces a distinct, specific error message rather than a
generic failure.

generic failure.

data.content: Now let's update `Troubleshooting.md` with entries for the new hint messages.

arguments.new_str:
## "l5xgit.exe not configured"

Shown as a warning card on the [[Main Window]] and as a status row in
[[Settings and Dependencies]]. Open **⚙ DEPENDENCIES** and either build the
tool (**Download + Compile Rockwell VCS Tools**) or point at an existing
compiled executable (**Use Existing l5xgit.exe**).

## Restore fails with "Could not find a part of the path ...RSLogix5000Content..."

The log panel now prints a `[hint]` block identifying this directly, instead
of only the raw `.NET` `DirectoryNotFoundException` stack trace, for example:

```
[hint] The exploded project content (RSLogix5000Content) was not found at the configured
[hint] 'Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path'.
[hint] Missing: C:\...\RSLogix5000Content\RSLogix5000Content.xml
[hint] That path must point DIRECTLY at the folder that contains the 'RSLogix5000Content'
[hint] folder — not the overall Git repository root, if the exploded project files live in a
[hint] subfolder of the repo (e.g. '<repo>\plc\exploded' rather than '<repo>').
[hint] Resolution: edit this controller mapping (EDIT button) and update the Git Repo /
[hint] Exploded Directory Path to the subfolder that directly contains RSLogix5000Content,
[hint] then try again.
```

**Cause:** the mapping's **Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path** points at the
Git repository root, but the exploded project content actually lives in a
subfolder of that repo (a common layout when a repo also holds docs,
scripts, or a separate binary ACD copy alongside the exploded source).

**Fix:** select the controller, click **EDIT**, and change the path to the
subfolder that directly contains `RSLogix5000Content`. See
[[Repository Mappings#what the exploded directory path must point to]] for
example folder layouts.

## Commit/Restore fails with "Required Logix Designer version: X.Y is not installed"

The log panel prints a `[hint]` block naming the exact required version
instead of only the raw exception, for example:

```
[hint] This ACD file requires Logix Designer version 20.1, which is not installed on this machine.
[hint] The ACD's authored version and the installed Logix Designer version must match exactly —
[hint] a newer installed version does not automatically open an older ACD's project data.
[hint] Resolution: install Studio 5000 / Logix Designer 20.1 side-by-side, or use an
[hint] ACD authored with a version you already have installed.
```

**Cause:** `l5xgit` opens the ACD via the Rockwell Logix Designer SDK, which
requires the exact Logix Designer version the ACD was authored/saved with to
be installed side-by-side — this is a vendor/licensing constraint, not
something this app can work around.

**Fix:** install the required Studio 5000 / Logix Designer version alongside
your current one, or use/author the ACD with a version you already have
installed.

tool (**Download + Compile Rockwell VCS Tools**) or point at an existing
compiled executable (**Use Existing l5xgit.exe**).

## Restore fails with "Could not find a part of the path ...RSLogix5000Content..."

The log panel now prints a `[hint]` block identifying this directly, instead
of only the raw `.NET` `DirectoryNotFoundException` stack trace, for example:

```
[hint] The exploded project content (RSLogix5000Content) was not found at the configured
[hint] 'Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path'.
[hint] Missing: C:\...\RSLogix5000Content\RSLogix5000Content.xml
[hint] That path must point DIRECTLY at the folder that contains the 'RSLogix5000Content'
[hint] folder — not the overall Git repository root, if the exploded project files live in a
[hint] subfolder of the repo (e.g. '<repo>\plc\exploded' rather than '<repo>').
[hint] Resolution: edit this controller mapping (EDIT button) and update the Git Repo /
[hint] Exploded Directory Path to the subfolder that directly contains RSLogix5000Content,
[hint] then try again.
```

Git repository root, but the exploded project content actually lives in a
subfolder of that repo (a common layout when a repo also holds docs,
scripts, or a separate binary ACD copy alongside the exploded source).

**Fix:** select the controller, click **EDIT**, and change the path to the
subfolder that directly contains `RSLogix5000Content`. See
[[Repository Mappings#what the exploded directory path must point to]] for
example folder layouts.

instead of only the raw exception, for example:

something this app can work around.

your current one, or use/author the ACD with a version you already have
installed.

arguments.new_str:
## Actionable error hints for known restore/commit failures

Triggered by a real "SHD-BOI-Line" restore failure where `l5xgit restoreacd` crashed with a raw
`System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException` stack trace mentioning `RSLogix5000Content` — root-caused to
the mapping's "Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path" pointing at the repo root instead of the
subfolder that actually contains the exploded project content. The user asked for in-app error
messages that explain the cause instead of requiring log/stack-trace literacy, plus docs tips on
the expected exploded-folder layout.

- [x] Add `L5xGitCliService.EmitExplodedPathMismatchHint`: detects
      `DirectoryNotFoundException`/`FileNotFoundException` stderr lines mentioning
      `RSLogix5000Content`, extracts the missing path, and prints a plain-language `[hint]` block
      naming the likely cause (wrong Exploded Directory Path) and the fix (point it at the
      subfolder that directly contains `RSLogix5000Content`).
- [x] Add `L5xGitCliService.EmitAcdVersionMismatchHint`: detects the "Required Logix Designer
      version: X.Y is not installed" message (encountered during the earlier full-process test
      session) and prints a `[hint]` block naming the exact required version and the fix (install
      that Logix Designer version side-by-side, or use an ACD authored with an installed version).
      This is a distinct failure mode from the existing `EmitLogixSdkCompatibilityHint` (SDK too
      old vs. ACD authored with a specific version not installed).
- [x] Wire both new hint emitters into the existing `ErrorDataReceived` handler in
      `RunProcessAsync`, alongside the pre-existing SDK-compatibility hint.
- [x] Update `docs/Repository Mappings.md` with a new "What the Exploded Directory Path must point
      to" section showing correct vs. incorrect folder layouts (repo root vs. a `plc\exploded`
      subfolder), and note the Add/Edit source-mode selector added in the prior session (was
      previously undocumented in the wiki, only in `README.md`).
- [x] Update `docs/Troubleshooting.md` with dedicated entries for both new hints, showing the
      exact `[hint]` output and the fix.
- [x] Update `README.md`'s feature bullet for stdout/stderr streaming to mention the hint behavior.

### Review

- Validation performed:
  - `dotnet build src\ABLogixGitManager\ABLogixGitManager.csproj -c Release` — passed, 0 warnings,
    0 errors (built to an isolated `-p:OutputPath` since the user's own running instance of the app
    held the normal output `.exe` locked during this session).
  - `dotnet test tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests\ABLogixGitManager.Tests.csproj` — **17/17 passing**,
    no regressions from the new private hint-detection helpers.
- Remaining risk:
  - No automated test exercises the two new hint emitters directly (they're `private static`, same
    as the pre-existing `EmitLogixSdkCompatibilityHint` they're modeled on, which also has no
    dedicated test) — verified by code review and build only, not by feeding a captured real
    stderr transcript through the method. Exposing them via `InternalsVisibleTo` for direct testing
    would be a reasonable follow-up if this pattern grows further.
  - Not re-verified against the user's real `SHD-BOI-Line` mapping in this session (would require
    reproducing their exact misconfigured path locally); the hint text was validated by hand
    against the literal stderr line reported in the bug report.

data.content:
Clean build. Here's a summary of what changed:

## What I found
The "no tracking information" logic wasn't the issue this time — the new error was a **path-configuration mismatch**: your `SHD-BOI-Line` mapping's "Git Repo / Exploded Directory Path" pointed at the repo root, but the actual exploded content lives at `plc\exploded\`. `l5xgit` crashed with a raw `DirectoryNotFoundException` stack trace instead of a useful message.

## What I changed

**In-app error hints** ([L5xGitCliService.cs](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/src/ABLogixGitManager/Services/L5xGitCliService.cs)) — extended the existing `[hint]` mechanism (previously only used for the Logix Designer SDK-too-old error) with two new detectors wired into the same stderr stream shown in the app's log panel:
- **`EmitExplodedPathMismatchHint`** — catches the `RSLogix5000Content`-not-found failure, prints the missing path, and tells the user to point the mapping's Exploded Directory Path at the correct subfolder instead of the repo root.
- **`EmitAcdVersionMismatchHint`** — catches "Required Logix Designer version: X.Y is not installed" (the error from your earlier full-process test) and names the exact required version with a fix.

Both now surface as plain-language guidance directly in the log panel instead of requiring the user to read/interpret a .NET stack trace.

**Docs**:
- [Repository Mappings.md](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/docs/Repository%20Mappings.md) — new "What the Exploded Directory Path must point to" section with correct-vs-incorrect folder layout examples (also caught up the Add/Edit dialog docs to the new source-mode selector from earlier this session, which had only been documented in README.md).
- [Troubleshooting.md](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/docs/Troubleshooting.md) — dedicated entries for both new hints with example output and fixes.
- [README.md](/c:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-Git/README.md) — updated the logging bullet to mention the hint behavior.

**Verification**: `dotnet build -c Release`/`-c Debug` — 0 warnings/errors (built to an isolated output path since your running instance held the normal `.exe` locked). `dotnet test` — 17/17 passing, no regressions.

**Residual risk**: the two new hint functions are `private static` (matching the existing pattern) and aren't covered by a dedicated unit test — verified by code/build review only, not a fed-in stderr transcript.
